habitat: Flocks on coastal islands, including artificial guano islands, and on estuaries, bays, lagoons and occasionally large dams.
summary: A common, localised resident. The non-breeding adult is all white, larger than Pink-backed Pelican, with a pale yellow and pink bill, a yellow bill-pouch and yellow legs. In flight the white underwings contrast with black flight feathers. The breeding adult has a pink flush, a yellow patch on the upper breast, a pink-and-grey upper mandible, a yellow pouch and pink legs. The colour key says pink legs and a yellowish bill. The immature has a dusky head and neck, dark brown wings and tail, and yellowish underparts. Newman does not describe the voice. The Kemp paper name White Pelican and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Pink-backed Pelican is smaller. Its colour key gives grey wings in non-breeding plumage, not an all-white body.

research.note: Newman calls it a common localised resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The colour key says pink legs, while the non-breeding sentence says yellow legs. That conflict, and the immature duskiness being only “various degrees”, is why this needs review. Population figures, the Kemp paper name White Pelican and the code NB were left unchanged.
